title: What Is Bariatric Surgery?
description: What bariatric surgery is, what it is for and which procedures it includes (sleeve, bypass, balloon). Care in Lima with price alternatives.
tldr: Bariatric surgery is a group of procedures to treat obesity and improve related conditions (diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea). It includes gastric sleeve, bypass and gastric balloon. At Cirugía 24 Horas it is performed in Lima with price alternatives by clinic; the specialist decides the indication.
bodyHtml:
Bariatric surgery groups the procedures that help treat obesity when diet and exercise have not been enough.

What is it for?

Besides weight loss, it can improve type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea and fatty liver. It is a medical treatment, not a cosmetic one.

Which procedures does it include?

The most common are the gastric sleeve, gastric bypass and gastric balloon. Each has different indications that the specialist determines.

At Cirugía 24 Horas

We operate in Lima with the same surgical team at different clinics, so you can choose the price alternative that fits you. We also care for patients from abroad.

faqs.a: No; it is a medical treatment for obesity and its related conditions.

faqs.q: Who decides which procedure is right for me?
faqs.a: The bariatric surgeon, after a multidisciplinary evaluation.

title: Types of Bariatric Surgery
description: Types of bariatric surgery: gastric sleeve, bypass and balloon. Differences, advantages and who each one is for.
tldr: The most common types of bariatric surgery are the gastric sleeve (removes part of the stomach), the bypass (small pouch plus intestinal reconnection) and the gastric balloon (a temporary, non-surgical device). The choice depends on BMI, health and goal, and is decided by the specialist.
bodyHtml:
Knowing the types of bariatric surgery helps you understand which option fits each patient.

Gastric sleeve

Removes about 70–80% of the stomach. A simple, widely used technique.

Gastric bypass

Creates a small pouch and reconnects the intestine; useful with diabetes or significant reflux.

Gastric balloon

A temporary device placed by endoscopy; for overweight or mild obesity.

Which one to choose?

It depends on BMI, related conditions and goal. The indication is medical.

faqs.q: Which one leads to the most weight loss?
faqs.a: Sleeve and bypass achieve more than the balloon; between the two, it depends on the case. The specialist decides.
No; it is endoscopic and temporary.

title: Am I a Candidate for Bariatric Surgery?
description: Criteria for being a candidate for bariatric surgery: BMI, related conditions and multidisciplinary evaluation.
keyword: am i a candidate for bariatric surgery
tldr: Usual candidates are people with a BMI of 40 or higher, or 35 or higher with related conditions (diabetes, high blood pressure, sleep apnea), without sustained results from medical treatment. Final candidacy is decided by the surgeon after a multidisciplinary evaluation.
bodyHtml:
Am I a candidate for bariatric surgery? That is the first question.

Usual criteria

A BMI of 40 or higher, or 35 or higher with related conditions, without sustained results from diet and exercise.

The evaluation

The surgeon, nutrition, psychology and, depending on the case, cardiology take part. It does not depend only on the patient's wishes.

Calculate your BMI and schedule a free evaluation.

faqs.q: What if my BMI is below 35?
faqs.a: Other options are prioritized; each case is evaluated individually.
General health is considered more than age on its own.

title: Risks and Complications of Bariatric Surgery
description: Possible risks and complications of bariatric surgery and how they are reduced with evaluation and follow-up.
tldr: Like any major surgery, bariatric surgery has risks: bleeding, staple-line leaks, infection, thrombosis and, with bypass, nutritional deficiencies. They are uncommon and are reduced with proper evaluation, careful technique and follow-up. The surgeon explains them during the consultation.
bodyHtml:
Learning about the risks of bariatric surgery is part of a responsible decision.

Possible complications

Bleeding, leaks along the staple line, infection, venous thrombosis and, especially with bypass, vitamin deficiencies.

How they are reduced

A complete pre-operative evaluation, careful laparoscopic technique, preventive measures and close follow-up. The team's experience matters.

faqs.a: It is widely performed; safety depends on the evaluation, the technique and the follow-up.

faqs.q: Will I need to take vitamins?
faqs.a: Bypass usually requires supplements; sleeve, as directed.

title: Recovery After Bariatric Surgery
description: What recovery from bariatric surgery looks like: timelines, staged diet, activity and check-ups.
tldr: Recovery from bariatric surgery is gradual: discharge in 1–3 days depending on the procedure, a staged diet (liquids, purees, solids), a return to light activities in 1–2 weeks and periodic check-ups. Timelines vary by patient and medical judgment.
bodyHtml:
Recovery from bariatric surgery happens in phases.

First days

Discharge in 1–3 days depending on the procedure, a liquid diet, hydration and gentle walks.

Following weeks

The diet advances to purees and solids, with a return to light activities and exercise as directed.

International patients

Your stay is planned to cover the first check-ups before you return home.

faqs.q: When do I go back to work?
faqs.a: Many patients resume in 1–2 weeks if the job is not physical.
After the first check-ups and the surgeon's approval.

title: How to Prepare for Bariatric Surgery
description: Preparing for bariatric surgery: tests, pre-operative diet, habits and emotional aspects.
keyword: how to prepare for bariatric surgery
tldr: Preparation includes completing the multidisciplinary evaluation and tests, following the prescribed pre-operative diet, stopping tobacco and certain medications as directed, and preparing emotionally. Good preparation reduces risks and improves recovery.
bodyHtml:
Preparation for bariatric surgery influences safety and outcome.

Before the operation

A multidisciplinary evaluation, pre-operative tests, the prescribed pre-operative diet, and stopping tobacco and certain medications.

Emotional preparation

Understanding the change in habits and having support improves adaptation afterward.

faqs.a: Weeks, to complete the evaluations and the pre-operative diet.

faqs.q: Do I need to quit smoking?
faqs.a: Yes; it reduces respiratory and wound-healing risks.

title: Sleeve vs Bypass vs Balloon: Which One to Choose
description: Comparison of gastric sleeve, bypass and gastric balloon: differences, advantages and who each one is for.
keyword: gastric sleeve vs bypass vs balloon
tldr: The balloon is temporary and non-surgical (overweight/mild obesity); the sleeve is a permanent surgery with good weight loss; the bypass is a surgery with a greater effect on diabetes and reflux. The choice depends on BMI, health and goal, and is decided by the specialist.
bodyHtml:
Sleeve, bypass or balloon? Each option has its place.

Balloon

Temporary and non-surgical; overweight or mild obesity, or a first step.

Sleeve

A permanent surgery with good, sustained weight loss; widely used.

Bypass

A surgery with a greater effect on diabetes and reflux.

How to choose

According to BMI, health and goal. The evaluation decides.

faqs.a: There is no single best one for everyone; it depends on your case.
Your preference counts, but the final indication is medical.

title: Bariatric Surgery Results: What to Expect
description: What results to expect from bariatric surgery, how soon and what they depend on. Realistic expectations.
tldr: After bariatric surgery, many patients lose a significant part of their excess weight in the first 12–18 months and see improvement in related conditions. Results vary from person to person and depend on sticking to new habits and on follow-up.
bodyHtml:
The results of bariatric surgery depend on each person.

What usually happens

Most of the weight loss happens in the first 12–18 months; diabetes, blood pressure and sleep apnea also tend to improve.

What it depends on

Your starting weight, how well you keep to your new habits, and follow-up. Surgery is a tool, not a substitute for lifestyle change.

Results vary from patient to patient.

faqs.a: Yes, if habits are not maintained; follow-up helps sustain the result.
In many cases it improves markedly, especially with bypass; it is individual.

title: Gastric Sleeve: What It Is and How It Is Done
description: Gastric sleeve (vertical gastrectomy): what it is, how it is done laparoscopically and who it is for. Price by clinic in Lima.
tldr: The gastric sleeve removes about 70–80% of the stomach laparoscopically, reducing how much you can eat and your appetite. It is permanent. At Cirugía 24 Horas it is performed in Lima with price alternatives by clinic; the specialist decides the indication.
bodyHtml:
The gastric sleeve (vertical gastrectomy) is one of the most commonly performed bariatric procedures.

How it is done

Laparoscopically: the side portion of the stomach is removed and a tube is formed. It reduces the amount of food and the hunger hormone.

Who it is for

Obesity according to BMI and risk; the specialist determines it.

Price

Alternatives by clinic, from low-cost options to all-inclusive. Free evaluation.

faqs.a: No; part of the stomach is removed permanently.
You are operated on under general anesthesia; discomfort afterward is manageable.

title: Gastric Bypass: What It Is and When It Is Indicated
description: Gastric bypass: what it is, how it works and when it is preferred (diabetes, reflux). Price by clinic in Lima.
tldr: Gastric bypass creates a small gastric pouch and reconnects the intestine, reducing food intake and absorption. It is often preferred with type 2 diabetes or significant reflux. It requires lifelong supplements. Price alternatives by clinic in Lima.
bodyHtml:
Gastric bypass is a well-established bariatric surgery.

How it works

A small gastric pouch plus reconnection of the small intestine. It reduces food intake and part of absorption.

When it is preferred

With type 2 diabetes or significant reflux, where it offers advantages.

Important

It requires lifelong supplements and check-ups. The specialist decides the indication.

faqs.a: It often improves it significantly in many patients; it is individual.

faqs.q: Is it more complex than the sleeve?
faqs.a: Technically yes; that is why the choice depends on the case.

title: Gastric Balloon: A Non-Surgical Option
description: Gastric balloon: what it is, how it is placed and who it is for. A temporary, non-surgical option for weight loss. Price by clinic.
tldr: The gastric balloon is a temporary device placed by endoscopy to create a feeling of fullness and help with weight loss, without surgery. It is usually removed after 6–12 months and comes with a nutrition plan. For overweight or mild obesity in selected cases.
bodyHtml:
The gastric balloon is a non-surgical alternative for selected cases.

How it is placed

By endoscopy with sedation, in a short outpatient procedure; it is filled once in place.

Who it is for

Overweight or mild obesity, or as a first step. It is temporary (6–12 months).

Key point

Pair it with healthy habits to maintain the result after removal.

faqs.a: No; it is placed by endoscopy, without incisions.
Yes; it is temporary and removed by endoscopy.

title: Anesthesia and Safety in Bariatric Surgery
description: What anesthesia is like in bariatric surgery and which safety measures are taken before, during and after.
tldr: Bariatric surgery is performed under general anesthesia, with the patient monitored by the anesthesiologist. Safety relies on the pre-operative evaluation (including cardiac and respiratory assessment), clot prevention and post-operative follow-up.
bodyHtml:
The anesthesia in bariatric surgery is general and is managed by the anesthesiologist.

Before

A cardiac and respiratory evaluation to reduce risks; fasting as directed.

During and after

Continuous monitoring, clot prevention and pain control. The length of stay depends on the procedure.

faqs.q: Will I feel pain during the operation?
faqs.a: No; you are asleep and monitored. Discomfort afterward is controlled.
Great care is taken with a prior evaluation, which is why it is essential.

title: Laparoscopic Bariatric Surgery: Advantages
description: What laparoscopic bariatric surgery is and its advantages: less pain, small scars and a shorter recovery.
tldr: Laparoscopic bariatric surgery is done through small incisions with a camera, instead of one large opening. Its advantages: less pain, lower risk of infection, small scars and a shorter recovery. It is the standard approach for sleeve and bypass.
bodyHtml:
Laparoscopic bariatric surgery is the standard technique today.

Advantages

Less pain, lower risk of infection, small scars and a quicker return to activities.

Is it for everyone?

Most people are candidates; the final decision depends on the surgeon's evaluation.

faqs.a: No; the incisions are small and the scars discreet.
It offers recovery advantages; safety depends on the team and the evaluation.

title: Diet After Bariatric Surgery
description: Staged diet after bariatric surgery: liquids, purees and solids, with protein, hydration and supplements.
tldr: After bariatric surgery the diet advances in stages: liquids, purees and solids, prioritizing protein and hydration in small portions, with vitamin supplements. The nutritionist personalizes the plan, and it is key to your results and recovery.
bodyHtml:
The diet after bariatric surgery is gradual and guided by a nutritionist.

Stages

Liquids → purees → solids over several weeks, as directed.

Priorities

Protein, hydration, small portions and supplements (vitamins, iron, calcium, B12), especially after bypass.

faqs.a: After several weeks, depending on your progress and instructions.
Yes; the plan should be personalized and supervised.

title: Warning Signs After Bariatric Surgery
description: Warning symptoms after bariatric surgery that need prompt medical attention.
tldr: After bariatric surgery, seek care without delay if you notice fever, severe or worsening abdominal pain, a rapid heart rate, difficulty breathing, persistent vomiting or bleeding. They may indicate complications that need prompt attention. Keep the team's contact details at hand.
bodyHtml:
Recognizing the warning signs lets you act in time.

Seek care without delay if there is

Fever, severe or worsening abdominal pain, a rapid heart rate, difficulty breathing, persistent vomiting or bleeding.

International patients

Direct contact with the coordinator and a plan for what to do before and after your return home.

faqs.q: Is shoulder pain a warning sign?
faqs.a: It is usually from the gas used in laparoscopy; if it is severe or persistent, seek advice.
The surgical team or emergency services, depending on severity.
